Quick one from our side as we look at H2 planning — we have about 150k committed inference units left in our current annual commitment, but usage is lumpy and we expect a mid-year burst for a pilot in Q4.

- Can Redwood convert a portion of the unused committed units into on-demand usage credits we can draw down (rather than losing them at renewal)? If yes, what conversion ratio do you typically use and how would that impact the committed price?

Subject: Re: Q: convert unused committed units to usage credits + short top-up

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers: yes (we can convert some committed units into usage credits) and yes (we support co-term top-ups).

High level options I recommend (I attached a quick pro-rata model):
1) Conversion voucher: move up to 50% of remaining committed units into a time-limited usage credit pool. Conversion ratio: 1 committed unit -> 0.9 usage credit (reflects committed vs on-demand economics). Credits expire at existing renewal date.
2) Mid-contract top-up: purchase additional committed units that will be annualized to Nov 1 (i.e., we pro-rate the price to co-term). For short commitments (<=3 months remaining) we offer a small administrative uplift (typically +3% fee) to keep operational overhead low.
3) Hybrid: convert a smaller % (e.g., 25%) to credits + buy a small top-up to cover the expected burst — keeps overall committed unit economics while giving you flexible runway.

I've proposed a few numbers in redwood_pro_rata_model_v2.xlsx that map your current remaining 150k units to the above options.

Next steps: if you prefer option 1 or hybrid, I can draft the amendment + credit memo for legal and billing to sign off. If procurement prefers firm numbers, loop in finance and we can prepare a one-page amendment and a DocuSign link.

cc: Marissa (pricing authority) and Ben (billing ops) to confirm approval windows.

— Karthik
